newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-FRANCE LEAD DAVIS CUP FINAL 2-1 AFTER TAKING DOUBLES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRANCE LEAD DAVIS CUP FINAL 2-1 AFTER TAKING DOUBLES.

text.p: France opened a 2-1 lead over Sweden in the Davis Cup final on Saturday when Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux won the doubles 6-3 1-6 6-3 6-3 over Jonas Bjorkman and Nicklas Kulti in a match of see-sawing fortunes.
Nerves played a key part in the match, with no player able to resist the palpable tension in the huge converted boat-building shed being used for the final.
Bjorkman, recently returned from a knee injury, was the most fragile, losing his first service game in the opening set and dropping it again three more times to allow the French pair through.
The experienced Forget, 31, and his 26-year-old partner wobbled in the second set, losing their deft touch at the net as the Swedes wrapped it up in just 24 minutes.
But the French roared back and won the next five games in a row as they took the third set before attacking Bjorkman again in the fourth.
The hapless Swede dropped his serve in the sixth and ninth games with Forget putting away a forehand cross-court winner.
The win left the Swedish favourites in a tight spot with Stefan Edberg, who twisted his ankle on Friday, doubtful for the reverse singles on Sunday.
